primary_claim: In Gradient Routing's GridWorld scalable-oversight experiment, a naive REINFORCE baseline with early stopping (using a small holdout set from the supervised episodes) performs on par with Gradient Routing, whereas the original paper's naive baseline (without early stopping) overfits/games oversight and underperforms.

effect.metric: ground-truth return in 5x5 GridWorld oversight task
effect.value: naive REINFORCE baseline with early stopping performs a little worse than GR at 1% oversight because naive's peak is lower than GR's peak, but is otherwise mostly on par with GR across oversight levels

depends_on: arXiv:2410.04332 (Gradient Routing: Masking Gradients to Localize Computation)
post: Weak-to-strong generalization - eliciting strong capabilities
arXiv:2410.05782 (Reinforcement Learning from Imperfect Corrective Action and Proxy Rewards)
contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies the original Gradient Routing paper's claim that GR outperforms naive REINFORCE baselines and data filtering in the GridWorld scalable oversight setting -- shows a stronger, regularized naive baseline closes most of the gap; also argues GR's setting is better characterized as semi-supervised RL with informational asymmetry rather than Scalable Oversight (Debate/IDA/RRM) or Weak-to-Strong Generalization
stated_future_work: Consider other baselines: training a reward model on supervised episodes then optimizing a stronger model against it on all episodes; penalizing mutual information between the oversight flag and agent's actions
limitations_stated: Early stopping relies on the assumption that supervised episodes can be split into train/holdout sets representative of the evaluation distribution, which becomes nontrivial in more complex settings
Early stopping reduces the number of labels available for training by reserving some for holdout
Performance still depends on early-stopping hyperparameters (patience, tolerance, min_steps)
quote: We reproduced these experiments and found that the naive baseline overfits, yet a simple regularization like early stopping (ES) makes the baseline perform mostly on-par with GR.
